scenarios.name: expansion-closure-and-manifestless
scenarios.purpose: Two launches of the same build differing only in what is staged: an expansion with a non-empty requires_oxps loads with its transitive closure and is refused without it, and a manifest-less in-tree fixture loads while emitting exactly its two standards errors.
scenarios.exercises: ResourceManager's search-path assembly, manifest.plist parsing, requirement resolution and the standards-diagnostic channel - as a COMPOSITION of expansions rather than one expansion in isolation.

distinct_from.007-012: each loads exactly ONE in-tree test-oxp, solo, and pins what its content does (JS, materials, shaders, PNG, AI, legacy missions). None stages a dependency closure, none carries a negative control in which the same expansion is REFUSED, and none pins the standards-error count of a fixture that has no manifest.plist at all.
distinct_from.001-006: no expansion is staged at all; the resource path under test here is not reached.

evidence_of_need: oo-kcrw proved causally that GNN alone is NOTLOADED with [oxp.requirementMissing] while GNN + Library is a PASS - a behaviour that exists today and that no golden pins.
oo-kcrw's NOMANIF state: five in-tree test-oxps ship no manifest.plist and emit exactly 2 [oxp-standards.error] lines each; that count is a load-path invariant nobody guards.
oo-het: a dead launch writes a log with zero ERROR lines, so this scenario's evidence must be a DIFFERENTIAL between two runs, not an absence.

extra.staged_control: the primary identifier alone, no closure
extra.manifestless_fixture: one of the five in-tree NOMANIF test-oxps, staged in both runs
extra.flight: none - the scenario stays docked, so the populator and the thrust-velocity problem are out of scope by construction

evidence.detail: the primary identifier appears in the [searchPaths.dumpAll] block of the CLOSURE run (ResourceManager.m)
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: the harness stages files and reads a log the engine writes; it never writes that block.

evidence.detail: the CONTROL run contains [oxp.requirementMissing] naming the primary, and the primary is ABSENT from its [searchPaths.dumpAll]
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: it is a line only ResourceManager emits, and it is asserted on the run that was deliberately under-staged - a harness that skipped the launch produces neither line.

evidence.detail: [startup.complete] present in BOTH runs (GameController.m): a progress marker emitted after expansion parsing
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: oo-het's exit-87 corpse carries the version banner and [process.args] but dies in display setup and never reaches this line.

evidence.detail: exactly 2 [oxp-standards.error] lines attributable to the manifest-less fixture, attributed per-expansion by tools/oxp_load_check.py
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: the count comes from OODebugStandards.m output; the harness only classifies lines it did not write.

evidence.detail: the exact closure list staged, written INTO the dump so the stored golden records what was loaded rather than trusting a capture-time assertion
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: it is compared against a freshly computed closure at diff time; a stale or hand-edited list differs by name.

not_evidence: absence of ERROR lines in Latest.log

cost.basis: two launches, both docked and neither flying: measured 10.4 s for the refused solo run and 14.8 s for the closure run, plus staging and dump round trips; the per-group figure from a 36-group tier run (18-22 s) is the independent cross-check.

red_means.symptom: the CONTROL run names the primary in [searchPaths.dumpAll]
red_means.meaning: requirement resolution stopped enforcing requires_oxps - expansions now load with unmet dependencies, which is how an OXP breaks silently for every user.
either the diagnostic channel died or the refusal moved earlier; in both cases the corpus tooling's verdicts become unattributable.

red_means.symptom: standards-error count for the NOMANIF fixture != 2
red_means.meaning: manifest parsing or the standards channel changed; a count above 2 means new complaints, below 2 means complaints were lost.
a dead launch - treat every other signal in that run as void.

red_means.symptom: the recomputed closure differs from evidence.staged_identifiers
red_means.meaning: the identifier index or the dependency walk changed; the run measured a different composition than the golden did.

scenarios.name: equipment-and-station-services
scenarios.purpose: Docked at the main station: award, query, damage and remove equipment, and buy one item - pinning the equipment registry, the OK/DAMAGED status machine, the station's tech-level-derived pricing and the resulting credit balance.
scenarios.exercises: OOEquipmentType, the equipment plist load, the award/remove/status paths on ShipEntity and the station's equipmentPriceFactor / equivalentTechLevel pricing - none of which any other tier reads.

distinct_from.001: pins the player LEDGER only (credits, legalStatus, score, cargo). The equipment array, the status machine and station pricing are absent from its dump.
distinct_from.004: is commodities: the market model and the cargo manifest. Equipment is a separate registry with separate pricing and a separate damage state.
distinct_from.003: damage in 003 is ship energy; equipment damage (EQUIPMENT_OK -> EQUIPMENT_DAMAGED) is a different state machine reached by a different call.
distinct_from.component-tier S1-S8: the component step library exposes only role counts and liveness; it cannot read an equipment array or a status string at all.

evidence_of_need: The dump schema in tests/golden/dump/dump_state.js carries entities, market, player ledger and cargo - there is no equipment field anywhere in any golden today.
Item 0.1 (iteration-order determinism) names equipment ordering as a prime suspect; the equipment array is the only place a golden could see that class of regression, and nothing looks at it.
This scenario never launches, so the populator interference that blocked oo-qwk5 and forced 001 to dump the smallest possible world does not apply - it is the cheapest defensible addition to the set.

extra.flight: none - docked for the whole run; undocked_seen is expected FALSE and is recorded as such rather than omitted
extra.equipment_key: one item that is damageable and not carry-multiple, named in the scenario spec so the golden pins a specific key rather than whatever was first in a list

evidence.detail: len(player.ship.equipment) after the award minus before == 1, and the awarded key is present in the array
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: Ship.equipment is READ-ONLY in the JS API (oxp-contract/js-api-1.93.json); the harness cannot write the array, only ask the engine to award.

evidence.detail: equipmentStatus(key) reads EQUIPMENT_OK, then EQUIPMENT_DAMAGED after setEquipmentStatus, and BOTH readings are stored in the dump
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: the second reading comes back from the engine's own equipment state after a write the engine may refuse; a broken status machine returns the first value twice.

evidence.detail: canAwardEquipment(key) returns false for a second award of a non-carry-multiple item
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: a REFUSAL is positive evidence the model is applying rules; a model that accepts every write returns true here.

evidence.detail: player.credits moves by exactly the price the engine computed for the purchase, and the price is stored alongside the delta
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: the harness records both numbers but computes neither; a pricing change makes them disagree by name in the diff.

evidence.detail: clock.absoluteSeconds advanced at least ticks * tick_seconds while docked, measured inside the game
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: it is the universe clock, which only advances while the run loop steps - a photograph of tick 0 fails it.

not_evidence: absence of ERROR lines in Latest.log
the equipment array being non-empty (the starting ship already has equipment)

cost.basis: one launch, no flight and no snapshot: 001 measured 24-32 s WITH a flight, a dock and a frame capture, so the same harness minus the flight is under that; the load itself is the 13.5 s term and the warm-launch figure is the floor.

red_means.symptom: the equipment array is unchanged after awardEquipment returned true
red_means.meaning: the award path no longer reaches the ship's equipment set - equipment can be bought and silently not installed.

red_means.symptom: equipmentStatus reads EQUIPMENT_OK after a damage write
red_means.meaning: the OK/DAMAGED state machine collapsed; damaged equipment would keep working, and the repair economy stops meaning anything.

red_means.symptom: canAwardEquipment returns true for a duplicate of a non-multiple item
red_means.meaning: rule enforcement in the equipment model was lost - the refusal branch is gone.

red_means.symptom: credits unchanged, or changed by an amount other than the stored price
red_means.meaning: the pricing path is dead or the formula moved; the diff names the field and the two numbers.

red_means.symptom: the equipment array is REORDERED with the same members
red_means.meaning: an enumeration-order regression in the equipment registry - exactly item 0.1's failure class, and this is the only scenario positioned to see it.

scenarios.name: hud-render-modes
scenarios.purpose: From one fixed camera pose in flight, render the same scene under three HUD modes (hud.plist, hud-small.plist, hidden) and assert the frame hashes agree within mode and differ between modes by more than the measured tolerance.
scenarios.exercises: The 2-D HUD drawing path and the dial definitions loaded from hud.plist / hud-small.plist - the only major rendering surface that no tier observes today.

distinct_from.001: its frame capture explicitly HIDES the HUD (frame_capture.apply_pose sets player.ship.hudHidden = true), so no golden in existence renders a HUD at all.
distinct_from.gui-tier-G1-G9: asserts that a window opened, took input and exited; it never compares what was drawn.
distinct_from.component-tier: asserts ship-state invariants over the console and never looks at a frame.
distinct_from.003: a combat scene differs in the 3-D scene; here the scene is byte-for-byte the same stimulus and ONLY the overlay changes, which is what isolates the HUD path.

evidence_of_need: oo-ae9 measured a usable tolerance (0.004377) with a 1.72x margin in both directions, and calibration.json records it; 001 consumes only the same-scene half. Nothing exercises the different-scene half as a standing assertion.

oo-ae9 also measured the instrument's blindness limit (a ship beyond ~400-800 m is below the noise floor), which is precisely why this scenario must calibrate its own stimulus before it may be blessed.
Every checklist and test-oxp scenario is a load-time assertion; the HUD path runs every frame of every session and is unobserved.

extra.populator: suppressed via system.setPopulator(key, null) as 001 does, so no traffic drifts into frame

evidence.detail: player.ship.hud reads back the requested plist name after the write, and player.ship.hudHidden is false for the two visible modes
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: an unapplied HUD write yields three renders of the SAME scene, which passes a within-mode check while measuring nothing - the same trap frame_capture.apply_pose already pays for on the camera pose.

evidence.detail: player.ship.docked is false and guiScreen reads GUI_SCREEN_MAIN at capture time
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: the HUD is not drawn on station screens; a docked capture would be a vacuous frame that agrees with itself perfectly.

evidence.detail: position read-back within 1.0 m of the declared pose, reusing apply_pose's assertion
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: the game reports the position it actually has; a silently unapplied pose differs by kilometres.

evidence.detail: every captured PNG exceeds 50 KB (a black frame is ~5 KB; real captures measured 300-343 KB)
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: a GL failure produces the black frame, and the floor sits an order of magnitude above it.

evidence.detail: the worst within-mode distance and the best between-mode distance are BOTH stored in the artifact, with the ratio asserted > 1 and both compared against calibration.json's tolerance
evidence.cannot_be_faked_because: the golden carries its own discrimination margin, so a later run cannot pass by shrinking the stimulus.

not_evidence: absence of ERROR lines in Latest.log
two captures being byte-identical (measured exact_match_rate is 0.0 - byte equality never holds here)

cost.basis: 6 captures (3 modes x 2 repeats) at the measured 26-28 s per capture, each in its own game process as the noise floor requires; the one-off separation calibration costs a further ~5 min, measured at 306.9 s for 11 captures.

measurement_risk.unknown: whether hud.plist and hud-small.plist differ by more than the tolerance measured for 3-D scene changes (0.004377) on a 960x720 llvmpipe surface. A HUD occupies a modest, mostly dark fraction of the frame, and oo-ae9 measured that a stimulus covering few pixels falls BELOW the noise floor.
measurement_risk.required_before_blessing: run the scenario's own calibration (3 modes x 3 repeats, each from its own game process) and record within-mode and between-mode populations in the artifact.
measurement_risk.if_populations_overlap: record NOT SEPARABLE at this surface, fall back to the largest stimulus pair (hidden vs hud.plist) and, if that also overlaps, mark the scenario INFEASIBLE at 960x720 and file the finding. Loosening the tolerance to make it pass is forbidden - that is the decoration oo-ae9's threshold work exists to prevent.

red_means.meaning: the HUD render became nondeterministic between processes, or rasteriser noise grew beyond what the calibration measured - re-measure the floor before touching the scenario.

red_means.symptom: between-mode distance falls below the tolerance
red_means.meaning: switching the HUD no longer changes what is drawn: dial definitions are not being loaded, or the overlay pass was skipped.

red_means.symptom: hud read-back does not match the requested plist
red_means.meaning: the HUD setter silently failed; every frame in that run is the same scene and the comparison is void.

red_means.symptom: docked is true or hudHidden is true at capture time
red_means.meaning: the run never reached flight, so the frames contain no HUD regardless of what they hash to.

red_means.symptom: a PNG below the byte floor
red_means.meaning: a black frame - GL initialised but nothing rendered; the whole run is void.

rejected_candidates.name: NPC AI-state census after a scripted provocation
rejected_candidates.why_wanted: the AI state machine is the single largest behavioural surface in the engine and no golden reads it.
rejected_candidates.why_rejected: Ship.AIState is permanently GLOBAL in this tier - addShips hands every ship oolite-nullAI.js while the player's scripts are not loaded (ShipEntityAI.m:254-257), and measured runs show zero setState hits. A dump field that is constant by construction is a fabricated field, not a measurement.
observables_missing: a per-ship AI-state read that can return anything other than GLOBAL in a harness-spawned world

rejected_candidates.name: Attack-versus-flee discrimination
rejected_candidates.why_wanted: the FLEE transition is, per the component-tier catalogue, the most commonly broken AI branch.
rejected_candidates.why_rejected: hasHostileTarget returns YES for FLEE as well as ATTACK, so the only exposed predicate cannot tell the two apart; a scenario built on it would go green on either behaviour.
observables_missing: Ship.isAttacking (the ATTACK side of the behaviour split), exposed symmetrically with isFleeing

rejected_candidates.name: Scenario-scoped survival of spawned ships
rejected_candidates.why_wanted: entity lifetime after destruction is where hand-translated refcounting is expected to fail first.
rejected_candidates.why_rejected: a role-count observable cannot distinguish a ship the scenario spawned from one the populator injected mid-run - oo-qwk5 measured pirate=2 at t=32.2 s with allShips going 10 -> 14 - and six beads have already reduced to this. A golden could suppress the populator, but the property still needs a HANDLE to the specific ships, which no observable provides.
observables_missing: a generic property read scoped to those handles

rejected_candidates.name: Moving-world determinism (a golden with ships under thrust)
rejected_candidates.why_wanted: 001 dumps a static world of 2 entities and 21 float literals, all exact binary fractions - thin evidence of engine-wide determinism.
rejected_candidates.why_rejected: a spawned ship under thrust reports velocity = newtonian + thrustVector (ShipEntity.m:12830-12833) and the JS setter reaches only the newtonian half, so no scenario can freeze it; -setTotalVelocity: is not exposed to JS. Measured: 4 of 6 ships still moving at 60-97 m/s immediately after the write, on 3 of 8 runs.
observables_missing: a JS seam for flightSpeed or setTotalVelocity, which has no bead yet - filing one is the prerequisite, not a scenario
